Suspension of operations by Kelly & Walsh Limited, (British),
No. 400 Ferry Road.
D.S.I. Smith,
E. A. Oda officer i/c.

Sir,
At 11 a.m. on the 23-1-42 a telephone message
was received from Mr. J.H. Searle, Director and Manager
of Kelly & Walsh Ltd., No. 400 Ferry Road, to the effect
that a number of dismissed workers were creating a
disturbance outside the premises.
D.S.I. Smith and a party of Police attended and
found approximately 50 dismissed workers congregated
outside the main entrance to the building. There was
no disorder.
As reported in Diary No. 1, the dismissed workers
were paid-off on the 31-12-41. They are now demanding
a "discharge gratuity" equivalent to 1 year's wages.
After it was explained to the disgruntled men that
the company had no funds available, and they would have
to wait pending further developments, they dispersed
quietly.

J. Smith
D.S.I.

(Signed) Officer i/c.

As a result of the present international situation Kelly
& Co. Ltd., No. 400 Perry Road, were compelled to suspend
operation of the 1-1-41.

Some 107 male and 10 female workers have been thrown-out
of employment. They were given their rice allowance for the
month of December but are not paid their wages owing to the
banking restriction.

At about 9.30 a.m. on the 31-12-41 some 80 workers
assembled outside the factory and demanded full pay for the
month of December and rice allowance for January 1942.

On the afternoon of the 31-12-41 Mr. J.H. Searle,
Director and Manager of Kelly & Co. Ltd., met six of the
worker representatives in Gordon Road Station, Detective
Office, and it was agreed between them that the workers shall
be paid today for the 12 days they have worked this month,
and when more funds are available they will receive the
balance of their December salaries and rice allowance for
January.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Since forwarding Diary No.2 on this case detectives
have interviewed Mr. Charlie Manager of Kelly & Walsh,
400 Nanking Road who states that all workers are
contented with their work nor do they appear satisfied
with their new positions.

Mr. Charlie pointed out that with the exception
of a few workers including Yung Foh Seu all his
employees are now standing with the firm and that
prior to everyone in these few, particularly above
named, there has been no trouble in the works therefore,
in view of the forcible attitude Yung Foh Seu adopted
when once his discharge was necessary he wished to have
a prosecution against him in Court.

Accordingly Yung Foh Seu has been charged with
intimidation contrary to Sec. 364 of the C.C.C. and will
reappear before Court on December 23rd for trial.

As there is insufficient evidence to prefer a
charge against the said undescribed Yao Jing Kwei, who,
incidentally made a statement on Dec. 18th implicating
Yung Foh Seu as the instigator of the strike, applica-
tion will be made for the cancellation of the Writ of
Detention against him.

自就本案发出第2号日志以来，侦探已约谈南京路400号凯利与沃尔什公司的经理查理（Charlie）先生，他表示所有工人均对工作内容感到满意，或者说他们似乎对新职位感到满意（原文此处逻辑似有矛盾，照实译出）。

查理先生指出，除包括杨福轩（Yung Foh Seu，音译）在内的少数几名工人外，他所有的雇员都站在公司一边；而在这些人，特别是上述指名者采取行动之前，工厂内并未发生任何纠纷。因此，鉴于杨福轩在其解雇必要时采取的强硬态度，他希望对其提起法庭诉讼。

据此，杨福轩被控违反《中华刑法典》第364条之恐吓罪，并将于12月23日出庭受审。

由于证据不足，无法对上述未详细描述之姚景贵（Yao Jing Kwei，音译）提出指控，顺便提一句，他在12月18日的一份陈述中指认杨福轩为罢工煽动者，故将申请撤销针对他的拘留令。

Enquiries by C.D.C. 120 and D.S.I. McChesney.

At 4.45 p.m., December 18th 1939 Mr. J. Searle
Manager of Kelly & Walsh Printers & Publishers
400 Ferry Road telephoned Gordon Road Station to
the effect that about 140 employees had at 2.30 p.m.
demanded a strike which was led by one particular
worker whom he wished to have arrested and charged.

A party of police visited the scene and on
investigation the strikers (Subject of Misc. File
No. 63C) ascertained that the workers had on about
December 15th made certain demands for better
treatment regarding rice allowance and bonus. The
management had at the time made it clear to the
workers that the demands would receive favourable
consideration but that same would require time, no
date being set for a reply to be given.

However, on the afternoon of December 18th
Mr. Searle left the office to make further investi-
gations regarding the dispute whereupon the accused
Yung Sun Chu (楊孫柱); at 2.30 p.m. (18th) ordered
all workers to cease work and stop machines.

Mr. Searle was contacted by telephone at 3.30
p.m. and returned at once to the works and enquired
the trouble. The accused demanded a reply to their
demands although he was not one of the representa-
tives of the workers signing the document of demands.

demands were receiving the attention of the directors
and that reply would be given as soon as considered.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the remainder of the striking workers becoming aware that Yung Poh Ou and Yao Ling Wei were detained over night a deputation of about ten proceeded to Haig Court Apartments where Mr. Earle resided with a view to requesting him to mediate with the police for the release of the two men. However Mr. Earle was absent and Mr. Allington, Assistant Manager visited Haig Court and persuaded the workers to wait until 7 a.m. 19th.

All workers gathered outside 400 Ferry Road after 7 a.m. and a representative party of six waited on Mr. Earle who gave his answer to the demands, that being

The Company will pay half the difference in price of rice per picul over $20.

Working hours are to be changed from present 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. to 8 a.m. - 8 p.m.

Ordinary pay for overtime instead of the present time and half.

The representatives consulted the workers and later requested mediation of Mr. Earle regarding the two arrested men. SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Gordon Road Station,
REPORT
Date July 24th. 1939.
Subject Strike of Workers at Kelly & Walsh Ltd., 400 Ferry Road.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey Forwarded by Officer i/c.

Sir,

On Saturday July 22, 1939 the undersigned received
information from Mr. J.H. Searle Managing Director of Kelly
& Walsh Ltd, 400 Ferry Road, to the effect that he expected
some labour trouble in the works.

Officer i/c Gordon Road was informed on Monday morning
24th and patrols in vicinity instructed to give above works
attention.

At 4.05 p.m. (24th) Mr. Searle informed the station
negotiations had broken down and that a "sit down strike" had
commenced at 4 p.m. The workers threatening to remain on
premises day and night until their demands were met.

Full particulars of strike and definite request of
management that the workers be ejected were explained to
D.O."B" Div. by Officer in charge when instructions were
received to eject if other means failed.

At 4.45 p.m. Inspt. White, S.I. Willis, D.S.I. McCahey,
D.S.I. Tao Keng Yong and a party of uniform and detective
staffs proceeded to the works at 400 Ferry Road and after
consultation with various workers, acting as spokesmen, an
amicable agreement was come to the effect that work would
continue normally until Thursday 10 a.m. July 27th, when
Management would deliver their reply to a representative
body of five or six workers, selected by the workers in the
office in presence of Police officers.

Workers then left the works quietly and Police returned
to station at 5.45 p.m.

In view of foregoing it is suggested an officer of the
Special Branch S.I. be in attendance at 10 a.m. Thursday
July 27th.

Yours obediently,

D.S.I.
D.D.O."B".

24日星期一上午，戈登路主管警官获悉此事，并指示附近巡逻队对上述工厂予以关注。

下午4:05（24日），西尔先生通知捕房，谈判破裂，并于下午4时开始了“静坐罢工”。工人威胁称，除非满足他们的要求，否则将日夜留在厂区内。

当接到指令称若其他方法失败则予以驱逐时，主管警官向B区警务总监解释了罢工的详细情况及管理层要求驱逐工人的明确请求。

随后工人安静地离开工厂，警务人员于下午5:45返回捕房。

此致，

副巡官
B区副总监。
